<x_0.1729><y_0.0594>**SECT. IV.** _Confervation of recent Vegetables and their Infusions, Ec. by Sugar and Honey._<x_0.9844><y_0.0938><class_Section-header>

<x_0.4414><y_0.0945>§ 1. CONSERVES.<x_0.7119><y_0.1109><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1719><y_0.1102>454. CONSERVES are compotitions of recent vege- table matters and fugar beaten together into an uni- form mafs.<x_0.9795><y_0.1531><class_Text>

<x_0.1699><y_0.1523>This management was introduced for preferving certain limples, undried, in an agreeable form, with as little alteration as poflible in their native virtues; and to fome subjects it is very advantageoufly applied. Vegetables, whole virtues are loft or deltroyed in dry- ing, may in this form be kept uninjured for a length of time: for, by carefully recuring the mouth of the containing veffel, the alteration, as well as diffipation, of their active principles, is generally prevented; and the fugar preserves them from the corruption which juicy vegetables would otherwise undergo.<x_0.9805><y_0.3055><class_Text>

<x_0.1689><y_0.3047>There are, however, fundry vegetables whose vir- tues are impaired by this treatment. Mucilaginous fulblances, by long lying with fugar, become leis glu- tinous, and affringents fentibly lofer upon the pa- late. Many of the fragrant flowers are of fo tender and delicate a texture, as almoft entirely to lofe their peculiar qualities on being beaten or bruifed.<x_0.9785><y_0.4023><class_Text>

<x_0.167><y_0.4016>In general, it is obvious, that in this form, on ac- count of the large admixture of fugar, only fulblances of confiderable activity can be taken to advantage as medicines. And indeed, conserves are at present con- fiidered chiefly as auxiliaires to medicines of greater efficacy, or as intermediums for joining them together. They are very convenient for reducing into bolufes or pills the more ponderosu powders, as mercurius dul- cis, the calces of iron, and other mineral preparations; which with liquid or lefs confluent matters, as fyrups, will not cohere.<x_0.9775><y_0.5523><class_Text>

<x_0.166><y_0.5516>The flops were formerly encumbered with many confers altogether infignificant; the few now retain- ed have in general either an agreeable flavour to re- commend them, or are capable of anfwering fome useful purposes as medicines. Their common dofe is the bulk of a nutmeg, or as much as can be taken up at once or twice upon the point of a knife. There is in general no great danger of exceeding in this particular.<x_0.9766><y_0.6773><class_Text>

<x_0.2432><y_0.6781>## 455. _General method of preferring conferences_.<x_0.8965><y_0.6969><class_Section-header>

<x_0.165><y_0.6961>Leaves are picked from the flalks, and flowers from their cups. They are beaten in a marble mortar, with a wooden petite, into a fmooth mafs; after which thrive their weight of double-refined fugar is added by degrees, and the beating continued till they are uniformly mixed.<x_0.9756><y_0.7836><class_Text>

<x_0.1631><y_0.7852>The fugar should be pulverified by itself, and patfed through a lieve, before it is mixed with the vegetable mafs; otherwise it cannot easily be reduced to fuifi- cient finenefs, fo as to be duly incorporated.
